options.en: the antibiotic imposes selection, so only plasmid-keeping cells live

quiz.explain_zh: 抗生素的唯一作用是杀死或抑制丢了质粒(因而丢了抗性基因)的细胞,形成选择压力,把保留质粒的那部分菌选出来。它不会与质粒结合、保护其序列不发生突变,不加快质粒在菌体内的复制,也不影响感受态细胞摄取质粒的转化效率——转化效率在加抗生素之前就已经决定了。
quiz.explain_en: The antibiotic's only role is to kill or inhibit cells that have lost the plasmid, and with it the resistance gene, so that selection keeps the plasmid-carrying fraction of the population. It does not bind the plasmid or shield its sequence from mutation, does not accelerate plasmid replication inside the cell, and does not affect uptake by competent cells — transformation efficiency is already fixed before any antibiotic is added.

quiz.q_zh: 严格来说,大肠杆菌获得质粒后属于哪种情况?
quiz.q_en: Strictly speaking, once E. coli acquires a plasmid, which statement is correct?

options.zh: 是“条件性的”,不带抗性基因的质粒就一定是瞬时的
options.en: “conditional”: a plasmid lacking a resistance gene is only transient

options.zh: 是“永久的”,但分裂中质粒仍可能因代谢负担丢失
options.en: “permanent”, yet the plasmid can still be lost as a metabolic burden

options.zh: 是“瞬时的”,几代之后质粒必然被完全丢失干净
options.en: “transient”, with the plasmid wholly lost within a few generations

options.zh: 是“永久的”,质粒在任何培养条件下都绝不会丢失
options.en: “permanent”, with the plasmid never lost under any culture setup

quiz.explain_zh: 获得质粒后的携带状态本身是稳定、可遗传的,可以叫“永久的”;但质粒对宿主是代谢负担,不加选择压力时分裂过程中总有一部分子代把它丢掉。这既不是几代之内必然丢光,也不是任何培养条件下都绝不丢失。是否携带抗性基因只决定能不能用抗生素施加选择压力,并不改变携带状态本身的性质。
quiz.explain_en: Once acquired, the carrier state is stable and heritable — fair to call it “permanent” — yet the plasmid is a metabolic burden, so without selection a fraction of daughter cells drops it at every division. That is neither guaranteed total loss within a few generations nor immunity to loss under every culture condition. Whether the plasmid carries a resistance gene only decides whether an antibiotic can impose selection; it does not change the nature of the carrier state.

title_zh: 【可跳过·非课程内容】生信合作、聚合酶结构与去哪个实验室的闲聊
title_en: [Skippable · not course material] Chat about bioinformatics collaboration, polymerase structures and lab choices

points.zh: 学生说自己生信不行，最多做点蛋白质序列的 BLAST，基因层面完全是门外汉，看不懂
points.en: The student says his bioinformatics is weak — at most protein-sequence BLAST; at the gene level he is a complete outsider.

points.zh: 老师的主项目就是病毒重组 (virus recombination)，实验室已发过一篇 Nature Communications（他是共同一作），这一篇他想冲 Nature 正刊，老板则提到可以先考虑 Nature Microbiology
points.en: The teacher's main project is virus recombination; the lab already published a Nature Communications paper (he is co-first author), and he wants this one in Nature itself, while his PI mentioned Nature Microbiology as an option.

points.zh: 他给学生看了一篇结构速递：武汉病毒所解析了克里米亚-刚果出血热病毒 (CCHFV) 聚合酶全酶 (holoenzyme) 的首个结构，“很大一坨”
points.en: He shows a structure news item: the Wuhan Institute of Virology solved the first full holoenzyme structure of the Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) polymerase — a very large complex.

points.zh: 顺带提到 Nature 很喜欢“背靠背”发表：两个不同课题组同一课题的研究同期发两篇
points.en: He notes Nature's fondness for back-to-back publication: two papers on the same topic from different groups in the same issue.

points.zh: 他所在的所里基本上你能想到的呼吸道病毒聚合酶都有人做，唯独新冠聚合酶没人接手——最早做的那几个人已经毕业走了，剩下的都在做当下正在流行的呼吸道疾病
points.en: At his institute essentially every respiratory-virus polymerase you can think of is covered, except the SARS-CoV-2 one: the people who worked on it have graduated, and those left work on currently circulating respiratory diseases.

points.zh: 流感病毒聚合酶有专门一个组在做，基本算世界上最强的之一；武汉病毒所的冷冻电镜 (cryo-EM) 也很厉害
points.en: One dedicated group works on influenza polymerase and is among the strongest in the world; WIV's cryo-EM work is also very strong.

points.zh: 学生对去武汉有顾虑（“以后自己要去哪”），只为发文章的话愿意去看看；老师建议也可以问问北大、清华做聚合酶的组
points.en: The student is hesitant about moving to Wuhan as a long-term choice, though willing if it is just for a paper; the teacher suggests also asking polymerase groups at Peking University and Tsinghua.

points.zh: 老师力邀学生加入自己实验室做项目：老板年纪轻、有三篇 Cell、惜才、对学生好，但坦言“这钱确实不多”，不必来做博后，先建立联系即可
points.en: The teacher urges the student to join his lab: a young PI with three Cell papers who values talent and treats students well — while being frank that the pay is low, so come for the collaboration rather than a postdoc.

points.zh: 学生表示开学以后再好好看看国内的项目，眼下先继续看书学习——随后课程正式恢复
points.en: The student says he will look at domestic projects once the semester starts and go back to studying for now — after which the lecture proper resumes.

extra.zh: 这里反复提到的“病毒聚合酶”对 RNA 病毒来说就是 RNA 依赖的 RNA 聚合酶 (RdRp)。它是宿主细胞没有的酶，因此是经典抗病毒药靶点：瑞德西韦 (remdesivir) 作为核苷类似物抑制新冠的 nsp12，法匹拉韦 (favipiravir) 同类机制作用于流感 RdRp。
extra.en: The "viral polymerase" repeatedly mentioned here is, for RNA viruses, the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp). Host cells have no such enzyme, which makes it a classic antiviral target: remdesivir is a nucleoside analogue inhibiting SARS-CoV-2 nsp12, and favipiravir works by the same kind of mechanism on influenza RdRp.

extra.zh: 冷冻电镜 (cryo-EM) 单颗粒重构之所以适合聚合酶全酶这种大分子机器：样品在玻璃态冰中速冻，不需要培养晶体，也不受晶格堆积限制，还能把同一样品里的多种构象分类重构出来——这正是“全酶结构”能被解析的技术前提。
extra.en: Why cryo-EM single-particle reconstruction suits large machines like a polymerase holoenzyme: the sample is flash-frozen in vitreous ice, so no crystals need to be grown and there is no crystal-packing constraint, and multiple conformations present in one sample can be classified and reconstructed separately — the technical precondition for solving a holoenzyme structure.

extra.zh: 学生提到的 BLAST 要分清工具：blastp 蛋白查蛋白，blastn 核酸查核酸，tblastn 用蛋白查核酸数据库的六框翻译。E-value 指在同样大小的数据库中偶然出现这么好比对的期望次数，越小越可信，它随数据库变大而变大。
extra.en: Distinguish the BLAST flavours the student mentions: blastp is protein vs protein, blastn nucleotide vs nucleotide, tblastn queries a nucleotide database with a protein by six-frame translation. The E-value is the expected number of hits this good arising by chance in a database of that size — smaller is more convincing, and it grows as the database grows.

quiz.q_zh: 瑞德西韦 (remdesivir) 抑制新冠病毒复制，其直接作用的靶蛋白是？
quiz.q_en: Remdesivir blocks SARS-CoV-2 replication. Which protein does it act on directly?

options.zh: 病毒的解旋酶/NTPase nsp13
options.en: the viral helicase and NTPase nsp13

options.zh: 病毒表面的刺突糖蛋白 S/spike
options.en: the viral surface spike glycoprotein S

options.zh: 病毒的 RNA 聚合酶亚基 nsp12
options.en: the viral RNA polymerase subunit nsp12

options.zh: 病毒的主蛋白酶 3CLpro/nsp5
options.en: the viral main protease 3CLpro/nsp5

quiz.explain_zh: 瑞德西韦是核苷类似物，被 RdRp 掺入新生 RNA 链后造成延迟链终止，直接作用的正是催化亚基 nsp12。主蛋白酶 3CLpro/nsp5 是奈玛特韦 (nirmatrelvir) 的靶点，解旋酶/NTPase nsp13 目前没有上市药物，刺突糖蛋白 S 则是中和抗体和疫苗的靶点。
quiz.explain_en: Remdesivir is a nucleoside analogue: the RdRp incorporates it into the nascent RNA and elongation stalls a few bases later, so the catalytic subunit nsp12 is what it acts on. The main protease 3CLpro/nsp5 is the target of nirmatrelvir, the helicase/NTPase nsp13 has no approved drug, and the spike glycoprotein S is what neutralising antibodies and vaccines aim at.

quiz.q_zh: 相对 X 射线晶体学，冷冻电镜单颗粒分析最主要的优势是？
quiz.q_en: Compared with X-ray crystallography, what is the main advantage of cryo-EM single-particle analysis?

options.zh: 可以直接读出蛋白质序列
options.en: it reads out the protein sequence directly

options.zh: 不需要对样品进行纯化
options.en: it needs no purification of the sample

options.zh: 不需要培养出蛋白质晶体
options.en: it needs no protein crystals to be grown

options.zh: 分辨率必定高于晶体学
options.en: its resolution always beats crystallography

quiz.explain_zh: 免于结晶是冷冻电镜的核心优势，大而柔性的复合物往往根本长不出晶体。它的分辨率并不保证更高（小蛋白仍是晶体学占优），蛋白质序列要靠测序或质谱确定，样品也仍然需要相当高的纯度。
quiz.explain_en: Escaping crystallisation is the core advantage — large, flexible complexes often never crystallise at all. Resolution is not guaranteed to be better (crystallography still wins for small proteins), the sequence still comes from sequencing or mass spectrometry, and the sample must still be quite pure.

title_zh: 第一代测序：桑格尔 (Sanger) 测序登场与三代测序技术的分代
title_en: First-generation sequencing: Sanger sequencing and how the sequencing generations are numbered

points.zh: 核酸这一章讲到序列测定，必须强调的是桑格尔测序 (Sanger sequencing)，1977 年问世，并因此获得诺贝尔奖
points.en: Within the nucleic-acid chapter, sequence determination comes down to Sanger sequencing, which appeared in 1977 and earned a Nobel Prize.

points.zh: 桑格尔测序就是所谓的“第一代测序”（一代 = Sanger）
points.en: Sanger sequencing is what is meant by "first-generation sequencing".

points.zh: 学生把“带荧光/带激光读碱基”的方法误认成 Sanger，老师纠正：那是二代测序，Sanger 的原理根本不是荧光检测
points.en: The student mistakes the "fluorescence/laser reads the bases" method for Sanger; the teacher corrects him — that is second-generation, and Sanger's principle is not fluorescence detection at all.

points.zh: 分代口径：一代 Sanger，二代是带荧光基团的测序，三代是纳米孔 (nanopore) 测序
points.en: The generations as stated: first is Sanger, second is fluorescence-based sequencing, third is nanopore sequencing.

points.zh: 老师提到自己的项目最近已经推进到差不多要去做纳米孔测序了
points.en: The teacher mentions his own project has advanced to the point of nearly doing nanopore sequencing.

points.zh: Sanger 测序用的关键试剂是双脱氧核苷三磷酸，即 ddNTP (dideoxynucleoside triphosphate)
points.en: The key reagent of Sanger sequencing is the dideoxynucleoside triphosphate, ddNTP.

points.zh: 尽管现在不再手工使用，Sanger 的原理仍是必须掌握的内容，因为它是所有测序方法的原型
points.en: Even though nobody runs it by hand any more, the Sanger principle still has to be known, since it is the prototype for all sequencing methods.

extra.zh: 年份要分清：Sanger 与 Coulson 的双脱氧链终止法发表于 1977 年；诺贝尔化学奖是 1980 年颁的，由 Sanger（他的第二座诺奖）与 Walter Gilbert、Paul Berg 分享。课上“1977 年并且获得了诺奖”是把两个年份压在了一起。
extra.en: Keep the two years apart: Sanger and Coulson published the dideoxy chain-termination method in 1977; the Nobel Prize in Chemistry came in 1980, shared by Sanger (his second Nobel) with Walter Gilbert and Paul Berg. The lecture's "1977 and it won the Nobel" compresses the two dates into one.

extra.zh: 第一代测序其实有两条并行的路线：Sanger 的双脱氧链终止法，和 Maxam-Gilbert 的化学降解法（用化学试剂在特定碱基处断裂末端标记的 DNA）。后者因为要用肼、二甲硫酸等剧毒试剂且不易自动化，被 Sanger 法完全取代——但两人 1980 年是一起得的奖。
extra.en: First-generation sequencing actually had two parallel routes: Sanger's dideoxy chain termination, and Maxam-Gilbert chemical degradation (cleaving end-labelled DNA at specific bases with chemicals). The latter was displaced entirely because it needs highly toxic reagents such as hydrazine and dimethyl sulfate and resists automation — but the two men shared the 1980 prize.

extra.zh: 今天测序公司说的“Sanger 测序”是荧光染料终止 (dye-terminator) + 毛细管电泳，四种 ddNTP 各带一种荧光、在一个管里反应。它带荧光，但仍然是第一代——分代的依据是“是否大规模并行”，不是“是否用荧光”。
extra.en: What sequencing companies call "Sanger sequencing" today is dye-terminator chemistry with capillary electrophoresis: the four ddNTPs each carry a different dye and react in a single tube. It uses fluorescence, yet it is still first generation — the generations are defined by whether reads are massively parallel, not by whether dyes are involved.

quiz.q_zh: 纳米孔 (nanopore) 测序判读碱基所依据的信号是？
quiz.q_en: What signal does nanopore sequencing use to call bases?

options.zh: 分子穿过孔道时的电流变化
options.en: the current change as a molecule passes the pore

options.zh: 每个碱基掺入时的荧光信号
options.en: the fluorescence emitted as each base is added

options.zh: 电泳中条带迁移距离的差异
options.en: the difference in band migration distance on a gel

options.zh: 终止片段在胶上的长度分布
options.en: the length distribution of the terminated fragments

quiz.explain_zh: 纳米孔测序让单链核酸穿过蛋白孔，不同碱基组合对离子电流的阻挡程度不同，直接读电流曲线即可定序，无需 PCR 扩增和荧光标记。掺入时发荧光是二代和荧光 Sanger 的读出方式，条带迁移距离和 ddNTP 终止片段的长度分布则都是电泳法的原理。
quiz.explain_en: Nanopore sequencing threads a single strand through a protein pore; different base combinations obstruct the ionic current differently, so the current trace itself gives the sequence, with no PCR amplification or dye labelling. Fluorescence on incorporation is how second-generation and dye-terminator Sanger read out, while band migration and the length distribution of ddNTP-terminated fragments are electrophoretic principles alike.

quiz.q_zh: 经典桑格尔测序区别于其他方法的核心试剂是？
quiz.q_en: Which reagent is the defining component of classic Sanger sequencing?

options.zh: 带可逆终止基团的荧光 dNTP
options.en: the reversibly terminating fluorescent dNTP

options.zh: 识别回文序列的内切酶 EcoRI
options.en: the palindrome-cutting endonuclease EcoRI

options.zh: 不依赖模板的末端转移酶 TdT
options.en: the template-free terminal transferase TdT

options.zh: 双脱氧核苷三磷酸 ddNTP
options.en: the dideoxynucleoside triphosphate ddNTP

quiz.explain_zh: ddNTP 缺 3′-羟基，掺入后链就停下来，这是 Sanger 法的全部关键。带可逆终止基团的荧光 dNTP 是 Illumina 二代测序的化学，成像后切掉封闭基团还能继续延伸；识别回文序列的 EcoRI 只负责把 DNA 切开，不依赖模板的 TdT 只在 3′ 端随机加尾，两者都产生不出定序信息。
quiz.explain_en: The ddNTP lacks a 3′-OH, so the chain stops as soon as it is incorporated — that is the whole trick of the Sanger method. Reversibly terminating fluorescent dNTPs are Illumina second-generation chemistry, where the blocking group is cleaved after imaging so extension resumes; the palindrome-cutting EcoRI merely opens DNA, and the template-independent TdT only adds a random tail to a 3′ end — neither yields any sequence information.

title_zh: ddNTP 的化学与四组平行反应：为什么掺进去链就断了
title_en: ddNTP chemistry and the four parallel reactions: why incorporation stops the chain

points.zh: ddNTP 把核糖上 2′ 位和 3′ 位的两个羟基全都去掉了，所以叫“双脱氧”
points.en: The ddNTP has had the hydroxyls at both the 2′ and the 3′ position of the sugar removed — hence "dideoxy".

points.zh: 正常核苷酸之间形成磷酸二酯键 (phosphodiester bond)：一端是 5′ 位的磷酸，另一端是前一个核苷酸 3′ 位的 OH
points.en: A normal phosphodiester bond joins the 5′-phosphate of the incoming nucleotide to the 3′-OH of the preceding one.

points.zh: 两个羟基都被取掉后，一旦在 PCR 过程中掺入，就不可能再往下连，整条链的延伸被停掉
points.en: With both hydroxyls gone, once it is incorporated during PCR nothing further can be attached and elongation of that chain stops.

points.zh: 操作体系：一段 DNA 模板 + 一条已知的引物 (primer)，做 PCR，加入四种普通原料 dATP、dGTP、dCTP、dTTP
points.en: The set-up: one DNA template plus one known primer, run as a PCR with all four ordinary substrates dATP, dGTP, dCTP and dTTP.

points.zh: 关键在于分成四组，每一组再额外加入一种对应的 ddNTP
points.en: The crucial step is splitting it into four reactions, each additionally receiving one of the four ddNTPs.

points.zh: ddNTP 不是百分之百掺入——普通的 dNTP 同时存在，所以它只是概率性地被偶然插入
points.en: The ddNTP is not incorporated every time: the ordinary dNTPs are present too, so incorporation happens only with some probability.

points.zh: 正因为是随机终止，同一组里会得到一系列长度不一的产物，每条都终止在同一种碱基上
points.en: Because termination is random, one reaction yields a whole series of products of different lengths, each ending at the same kind of base.

points.zh: 四组用一模一样的程序扩增，最后把四组产物一起拿去跑一块胶
points.en: All four reactions are amplified with an identical programme, and the four products are then run together on one gel.

extra.zh: 老师在讲测序时反复把核苷酸 (nucleotide) 说成“氨基酸”，例如“每组加一种滴滴的这个氨基酸”。他在同一句里就改口成“滴滴的核苷酸”(01:40:49)，随后在 01:41:20 和 01:44:57 也各改口一次，但 01:43:24、01:44:26、01:46:33 仍然说成氨基酸。测序读的自始至终是 nucleotide 序列，氨基酸是蛋白质的单体，要靠翻译才出现。
extra.en: Throughout the sequencing section the teacher repeatedly says "amino acid" where he means nucleotide, e.g. "each tube gets one dd-amino acid". He corrects himself within the same sentence to "dd-nucleotide" (01:40:49) and again at 01:41:20 and 01:44:57, but says amino acid again at 01:43:24, 01:44:26 and 01:46:33. Sequencing reads a nucleotide sequence throughout; amino acids are the monomers of protein and only appear after translation.

extra.zh: “双脱氧”是相对核糖 (ribose) 讲的：DNA 用的脱氧核苷酸本来 2′ 位就没有羟基，所以 ddNTP 与 dNTP 之间唯一有功能意义的差别是缺少 3′-OH。考试问“为什么终止”，答案只能落在 3′-羟基上，不能答 2′。
extra.en: "Dideoxy" is stated relative to ribose: the deoxynucleotides used in DNA already lack the 2′-OH, so the only functionally meaningful difference between a ddNTP and a dNTP is the missing 3′-OH. When an exam asks why the chain terminates, the answer must be the 3′-hydroxyl, never the 2′.

extra.zh: ddNTP 与 dNTP 的浓度比决定终止产物的长度分布：ddNTP 比例越高，终止越早、短片段越多、可读长度越短；比例越低则产物越长但近引物端的条带太弱读不出来。实际配方要在两者之间折中，这也是为什么 Sanger 读长有上限而不是想读多长读多长。
extra.en: The ddNTP:dNTP ratio sets the length distribution of the terminated products: more ddNTP means earlier termination, more short fragments and a shorter usable read; less ddNTP gives longer products but bands near the primer too faint to call. Real recipes compromise between the two, which is why a Sanger read has an upper length limit rather than running as far as you like.

quiz.q_zh: ddNTP 掺入后使 DNA 链延伸终止，直接原因是？
quiz.q_en: Why does an incorporated ddNTP stop chain elongation?

options.zh: 缺 3′-羟基，无法形成磷酸二酯键
options.en: no 3′-OH, so no phosphodiester bond can form

options.zh: 缺 5′-磷酸，无法被聚合酶所识别
options.en: no 5′-phosphate, so the polymerase ignores it

options.zh: 碱基配对发生错误，使聚合酶脱落
options.en: it mispairs badly, so the polymerase falls off

options.zh: 三磷酸基团无法水解，不能供能量
options.en: its triphosphate cannot be hydrolysed for energy

quiz.explain_zh: 延伸靠新加核苷酸的 5′-磷酸与链末端 3′-OH 缩合，ddNTP 恰恰没有 3′-OH，所以自己能被接上、却接不上下一个。它的 5′ 三磷酸完好、能被聚合酶正常识别，碱基配对也完全正确、不会让聚合酶脱落，三磷酸水解供能同样照常进行——这正是它能被掺入的前提。
quiz.explain_en: Elongation condenses the 5′-phosphate of the incoming nucleotide with the 3′-OH at the chain end, and the ddNTP has exactly no 3′-OH — so it can be added but nothing can be added after it. Its 5′-triphosphate is intact and recognised normally, its base pairing is entirely correct and does not shed the polymerase, and hydrolysis of the triphosphate still supplies energy — which is precisely why it gets incorporated at all.

quiz.q_zh: 经典 Sanger 反应分四管，每一管中加入的核苷酸原料是？
quiz.q_en: In the classic four-tube Sanger reaction, what nucleotide substrates go into each tube?

options.zh: 四种 dNTP 齐全，另加一种 ddNTP
options.en: all four dNTPs present, plus one ddNTP

options.zh: 四种 ddNTP 全加，完全不加 dNTP
options.en: all four ddNTPs added and no dNTP at all

options.zh: 四种 ddNTP 齐全，另加一种 dNTP
options.en: all four ddNTPs present, plus one dNTP

options.zh: 只加一种 ddNTP，完全不加 dNTP
options.en: just one ddNTP added and no dNTP at all

quiz.explain_zh: 四种普通 dNTP 必须齐全，链才能一直延伸下去；每管只额外加一种 ddNTP，才能让“在某个长度处终止”唯一对应某一种碱基。一个 dNTP 都不加、或者把四种 ddNTP 全加进去，链刚接上一个碱基就停住，得不到长度阶梯；把 dNTP 与 ddNTP 的角色对调同样只会得到一堆无法解读的极短片段。
quiz.explain_en: All four ordinary dNTPs must be present or the chain cannot keep extending, and only a single ddNTP goes into each tube so that "terminated at this length" maps uniquely onto one kind of base. Leaving the dNTPs out entirely, or putting all four ddNTPs in, stops every chain after a single added base and yields no ladder; swapping the roles of dNTP and ddNTP gives the same useless pile of ultra-short fragments.

title_zh: 读胶：条带阶梯、互补配对，以及回到模板的 5′→3′ 换算
title_en: Reading the gel: the band ladder, base pairing, and converting back to the template's 5′→3′

points.zh: 四组产物并排电泳，得到一系列相差一个碱基的条带，就是所谓的测序阶梯
points.en: The four reactions are run side by side, giving a series of bands one base apart — the sequencing ladder.

points.zh: 分离依据是分子大小：越小的片段跑得越快跑得越远，越大的跑得越慢
points.en: Separation is by size: smaller fragments run faster and further, larger ones run slower.

points.zh: 读法是从最短的片段开始，沿着延伸的方向一条一条往上读
points.en: You read from the shortest fragment upward, following the direction of extension.

points.zh: 某个位置的条带出现在加 ddC 的那一组，说明新合成链此处是 C，那么原始模板上与它配对的就是 G
points.en: If the band at a given position sits in the ddC lane, the newly made strand has a C there, so the template it pairs with has a G.

points.zh: 课上按图从小到大读出的例子是 C、A、G、T、A，长度每次增加一个碱基
points.en: Working up the figure from the smallest, the lecture reads out C, A, G, T, A, each band one base longer.

points.zh: 方向约定：课上假定模板是 3′→5′ 排布，那么引物延伸出的新链方向就是 5′→3′
points.en: Direction convention: the lecture assumes the template is laid out 3′→5′, so the new strand extending from the primer runs 5′→3′.

points.zh: 要把读到的新链序列换算回原本的 DNA 模板，必须做两件事：碱基互补 (C 对 G、A 对 T)，并把方向反过来
points.en: To convert the read-out of the new strand back to the original template you must do two things: complement each base (C with G, A with T) and reverse the direction.

points.zh: 之所以要反向，是因为 DNA 序列的书写和命名习惯一律是从 5′ 端写到 3′ 端，而读胶的方向与之相反
points.en: The reversal is needed because DNA sequences are always written and named 5′ to 3′, whereas the gel is read in the opposite orientation.

extra.zh: 课上把这块胶说成“琼脂糖 (agarose) 凝胶”。要达到单碱基分辨率必须用变性聚丙烯酰胺凝胶 (denaturing polyacrylamide gel，含尿素、常配甲酰胺上样并加热变性)；琼脂糖孔径太大，分不开相差 1 bp 的片段，一般只能分辨几十到上百 bp 的差别。这一点也正是后面那块半米长胶存在的理由。
extra.en: The lecture calls the gel an agarose gel. Single-base resolution requires a denaturing polyacrylamide gel (with urea, typically loaded in formamide and heat-denatured); agarose has far too large a pore size to separate fragments differing by 1 bp and normally resolves only tens to hundreds of bp. This is also exactly why the half-metre gel described later had to exist.

extra.zh: 电泳的方向和读胶的方向要分开：DNA 带负电，从上方加样孔向下（向正极）泳动，小片段跑得更远、停在胶的下部。所以“从下往上读”读的是从短到长，即新链的 5′→3′ 方向。课上说成“从下面往上跑”是把泳动方向说反了，结论（从下往上读）本身是对的。
extra.en: Keep the running direction and the reading direction apart: DNA is negatively charged and migrates downward from the loading well toward the anode, so small fragments travel further and end up low in the gel. Reading bottom to top therefore goes short to long, i.e. 5′→3′ along the new strand. The lecture's "it runs from the bottom upward" inverts the migration direction, though its conclusion — read from the bottom up — is right.

extra.zh: 由新链推模板，标准操作是取反向互补 (reverse complement)。考试里最常见的失分是只做互补不反向、或只反向不做互补，两者都会给出一条并不存在的序列。检验的办法：写完后把模板与新链上下对齐，两端的 5′ 必须分别在左右两侧（反向平行 antiparallel）。
extra.en: Deriving the template from the new strand means taking the reverse complement. The commonest exam slip is complementing without reversing, or reversing without complementing — either produces a sequence that does not exist. A quick check: write the two strands one above the other; their 5′ ends must sit at opposite ends (antiparallel).

quiz.q_zh: 在加 ddCTP 的那一组中，某一长度处出现条带。原始模板链在该位置的碱基是？
quiz.q_en: A band appears at a given length in the ddCTP reaction. Which base sits at that position on the original template strand?

options.zh: T
options.en: T

options.zh: G
options.en: G

options.zh: C
options.en: C

options.zh: A
options.en: A

quiz.explain_zh: ddC 能在此处掺入，说明新合成链该位置是 C；按碱基互补配对，模板上与 C 配对的必然是 G。答 C 是把新链当成了模板，答 A 或 T 则与 C 根本不配对。
quiz.explain_en: That ddC was incorporated there means the newly synthesised strand carries a C at that position, and by base pairing the template must carry a G. Answering C mistakes the new strand for the template, while A or T do not pair with C at all.

quiz.q_zh: 已从测序胶读出新合成链的序列，要写出模板链的序列，正确做法是？
quiz.q_en: Having read the new strand off the gel, how do you write down the template strand?

options.zh: 只取互补，不改变方向
options.en: complement it, keeping the direction

options.zh: 只反向排列，不取互补
options.en: reverse the order but keep the bases

options.zh: 原样照抄，不做改动
options.en: copy it out exactly as it was read

options.zh: 同时取互补并反向排列
options.en: complement it and reverse the order

quiz.explain_zh: 两条链既互补又反向平行，所以互补和反向必须同时做。只取互补而不改方向，会把 5′ 端和 3′ 端标反；只反向排列而不换碱基，得到的碱基根本不对；原样照抄写下来的仍是新合成链，而不是模板链。
quiz.explain_en: The two strands are complementary as well as antiparallel, so each operation is required. Complementing without changing direction labels the 5′ and 3′ ends the wrong way round, reversing the order while keeping the bases leaves entirely the wrong bases, and copying it out verbatim still gives the newly made strand rather than the template.

title_zh: 终止法的实操代价：半米长胶、通宵电泳、肉眼读带，以及带荧光的自动测序
title_en: What running the chain-termination method actually cost: half-metre gels, overnight runs, reading bands by eye, and fluorescent automated sequencing

points.zh: 这个方法之所以又叫终止法 (chain-termination method)，就是因为 ddNTP 插进去以后这段序列没办法被进一步 PCR 延伸
points.en: The method is also called the chain-termination method precisely because once the ddNTP goes in, that chain can no longer be extended by PCR.

points.zh: 现在不会有人再去手工做这个实验了，因为它极度考验操作手法
points.en: Nobody performs this experiment by hand any more, because it makes extreme demands on technique.

points.zh: 它用的不是常见的那种跑几十 bp 到几千 bp、只有五厘米见方的小胶
points.en: It does not use the familiar little five-centimetre square gel for fragments of tens to thousands of bp.

points.zh: 它用的是高 50 厘米、半米长的巨大凝胶
points.en: It uses a huge gel fifty centimetres tall — half a metre long.

points.zh: 之所以要这么长，是因为分辨率必须做到 1 bp：相差一个碱基的两条片段都要能分开
points.en: That length is needed because the resolution has to reach 1 bp: two fragments differing by a single base must be separated.

points.zh: 老师听上课时说过，这种胶有时要跑几个小时甚至通宵过夜，让条带一点一点慢慢分开
points.en: As the teacher heard in class, such gels sometimes ran for hours or overnight, letting the bands separate slowly.

points.zh: 跑完还要给胶拍照、用肉眼一条一条读带、再人工把序列拼装起来
points.en: After the run you still had to photograph the gel, call every band by eye, and assemble the sequence by hand.

points.zh: 读几十个碱基还行，几百、几千个碱基用手工 Sanger 法读，人要读废掉
points.en: A few dozen bases is manageable; reading hundreds or thousands this way would destroy the person doing it.

points.zh: 公司现在用的是碱基上带荧光基团的方法：四种碱基各带不同的荧光基团、发特定波长的光，PCR 时每接上一个碱基就发出对应波长的光，仪器读光就能快速定序
points.en: Companies now use bases carrying fluorophores: the four bases carry different fluorophores emitting at specific wavelengths, so as each base is added a particular wavelength is emitted and the machine reads the light to call the sequence quickly.

extra.tag: 课上说法不同 · lecture states it differently
extra.zh: 老师把测序公司的荧光法笼统归为“二代”。实际上公司做单样本 Sanger 服务用的是荧光染料终止 + 毛细管电泳，仍属第一代自动化，读长可到几百碱基；真正的二代 (如 Illumina) 是在芯片上形成 DNA 簇，用可逆终止的荧光 dNTP 一轮一轮“加碱基—成像—切除封闭基团”，同时读几亿条短序列。而“每掺入一个碱基就实时发一次光”更接近焦磷酸测序 (pyrosequencing) 或三代的 PacBio SMRT，不是 Illumina 的机制。
extra.en: The teacher lumps the companies' fluorescent method into "second generation". In fact a single-sample Sanger service uses dye terminators with capillary electrophoresis — still automated first generation, with reads of a few hundred bases. True second generation (Illumina) grows DNA clusters on a flow cell and cycles "add reversibly terminated fluorescent dNTP — image — cleave the block", reading hundreds of millions of short sequences at once. Emitting light in real time as each base is added is closer to pyrosequencing or third-generation PacBio SMRT, not Illumina.

extra.zh: 这一段里的“几十个氨基酸、几百个氨基酸、几千氨基酸”指的都是核苷酸/碱基数，不是氨基酸——测序测的是核酸链长。此外老师用 “base pair” 指单个碱基：“一个 base pair 上面带一段荧光基团”应为一个 base (碱基)：测序反应里延伸的是单链，bp 是双链的计数单位。
extra.en: The "tens / hundreds / thousands of amino acids" in this passage all mean nucleotides or bases — sequencing measures the length of a nucleic-acid chain. He also uses "base pair" for a single base: "a fluorophore on each base pair" should be on each base, since the sequencing reaction extends a single strand and bp is a unit for double-stranded DNA.

extra.zh: 一次 Sanger 反应的可读长度大约在几百个碱基（常规约 700–900 bp，起始几十个碱基因条带拥挤而质量差）。这既解释了为什么“几千个碱基”必须分段测序再拼接，也解释了为什么需要那么长的胶——读长上限本质上由电泳能否分开长片段决定。
extra.en: One Sanger reaction reads a few hundred bases (routinely about 700–900 bp, with the first few dozen bases poor because the bands are crowded). That explains both why thousands of bases must be sequenced in segments and reassembled, and why the gel had to be so long — the read-length ceiling is essentially set by whether electrophoresis can still separate the long fragments.

quiz.q_zh: 手工 Sanger 测序必须使用半米长凝胶，根本原因是？
quiz.q_en: Why did manual Sanger sequencing require a half-metre gel?

options.zh: 要避免四种荧光信号相互干扰
options.en: to stop the four fluorescent dyes interfering

options.zh: 要分开只相差一个碱基的片段
options.en: to resolve fragments that differ by one base

options.zh: 要容纳四组样品的全部加样孔
options.en: to fit the loading wells for four reactions

options.zh: 要让电泳电压保持在很低水平
options.en: to keep the electrophoresis voltage very low

quiz.explain_zh: 阶梯上相邻两条带只差一个核苷酸，要把它们在空间上分开就必须延长迁移距离，所以胶要极长、还常常通宵慢跑。加样孔只需四个泳道，那是宽度问题而非长度问题；电压和荧光干扰都与经典手工 Sanger 的放射性同位素读带无关。
quiz.explain_en: Neighbouring bands on the ladder differ by a single nucleotide, and separating them in space demands a long migration distance — hence an extremely long gel run slowly, often overnight. Four lanes of wells is a question of width, not length, and voltage or dye crosstalk have nothing to do with classic manual Sanger, which was read from radioactive labels.

quiz.q_zh: 测序公司提供的常规“Sanger 测序”服务，其技术归属和读出方式是？
quiz.q_en: How should a sequencing company's routine "Sanger sequencing" service be classified, and how does it read out?

options.zh: 二代：芯片上大规模并行合成
options.en: second-gen: massively parallel on a chip

options.zh: 三代：纳米孔电流信号读取
options.en: third-gen: nanopore current signal read

options.zh: 二代：焦磷酸实时发光检测
options.en: second-gen: real-time pyrosequencing light

options.zh: 一代：荧光终止加毛细管电泳
options.en: first-gen: dye terminators, capillary run

quiz.explain_zh: 公司做的仍是双脱氧终止反应，只是四种 ddNTP 各带一种荧光染料、在一根毛细管里电泳分离，因此它仍归入一代测序，只是把读带过程自动化了。芯片上并行合成是 Illumina，纳米孔电流是三代，焦磷酸发光是 454 的化学，三者都不产生 ddNTP 终止的长度阶梯。
quiz.explain_en: The company still runs a dideoxy termination reaction; only now the four ddNTPs each carry a dye and are separated in a capillary, which makes it automated first generation. Parallel synthesis on a chip is Illumina, nanopore current is third generation, and pyrosequencing light was 454 chemistry — none of them produces a ddNTP-terminated length ladder.

title_zh: 静态化学收尾，进入动态生物化学：代谢总论与合成/分解代谢
title_en: Closing static biochemistry and opening the dynamic half: what metabolism is, anabolism vs catabolism

points.zh: 接下来的 PCR 一节（变性、退火、延伸）不用看了，已经很耳熟；DNA 的化学合成一节也不用看，完全过时，公司现在都用更新的合成方法
points.en: The PCR section (denaturation, annealing, extension) can be skipped as too familiar, and the chemical synthesis of DNA is skipped as thoroughly obsolete — companies use much newer synthesis methods.

points.zh: 至此所有静态生物化学讲完，开始进入动态生物化学，今天先把这一章开个头
points.en: That closes all of static biochemistry; the dynamic half begins here, with today covering just the opening of the chapter.

points.zh: 本节要讲的是两个总论：代谢总论，以及生物能学 / 代谢能学的总论
points.en: This session covers two overviews: an overview of metabolism, and one of bioenergetics.

points.zh: 下节课开始进入第一个“真正的大魔王”——三羧酸循环 (TCA cycle)
points.en: The next session enters the first genuinely hard topic — the TCA cycle.

points.zh: 老师和学生都强调动态部分必须中英文对照学：这一块全部是酶，只学中文会串
points.en: Both teacher and student stress studying the dynamic half in Chinese and English together: it is all enzymes, and Chinese alone gets them tangled.

points.zh: 中文生化的一个麻烦：很多酶的中文名字彼此非常像，而且同一个反应的正、反方向往往是不同的酶，底物和产物却一模一样，非常难记
points.en: A real nuisance of Chinese biochemistry: many enzyme names look nearly alike, and the forward and reverse directions of one reaction are often different enzymes with identical substrates and products — hard to keep straight.

points.zh: 代谢 (metabolism) 指生物体与周围环境进行物质、能量交换的过程，统称新陈代谢
points.en: Metabolism means the exchange of matter and energy between an organism and its surroundings, collectively called 新陈代谢.

points.zh: 能否进行新陈代谢正是我们用来定义“一个生命之所以是生命”的标准
points.en: Whether something carries out metabolism is exactly the criterion used to define a living thing as living.

points.zh: 课上给的比例：约 99% 的生命体合成代谢大于分解代谢；例外是分解者——那些小细菌体内分解代谢高于合成代谢
points.en: The figure given in class: in roughly 99% of organisms anabolism exceeds catabolism; the exception is the decomposers, those small bacteria in which catabolism runs higher than anabolism.

extra.tag: 课上说法不同 · lecture states it differently
extra.zh: “99% 的生命合成代谢大于分解代谢”只对处在生长期、净增重的个体成立。成年个体处于能量平衡时，合成与分解速率大致相等，蛋白质等大分子处于持续的更新周转 (turnover) 状态——净合成大于净分解意味着长个子或增重，净分解大于净合成则是消瘦。所以更稳妥的说法是“两者动态平衡，方向随生长状态和营养状态变化”。
extra.en: "Anabolism exceeds catabolism in 99% of life" holds only for growing organisms with net mass gain. In an adult in energy balance the two run at roughly equal rates, with macromolecules such as proteins in continuous turnover — net anabolism means growth or weight gain, net catabolism means wasting. The safer statement is that the two are in dynamic balance, with the direction set by growth stage and nutritional state.

extra.zh: 两者的标准对照：合成代谢 (anabolism) 由小分子建成大分子，耗能、是还原性过程，主要还原力是 NADPH；分解代谢 (catabolism) 把大分子降解为小分子，产能、是氧化性过程，主要产物是 NADH 和 FADH2。这一区分正是后面判断“某条通路用哪种辅酶”的依据。
extra.en: The standard contrast: anabolism builds large molecules from small ones — it consumes energy, is reductive, and draws its reducing power mainly from NADPH; catabolism degrades large molecules to small ones — it releases energy, is oxidative, and yields mainly NADH and FADH2. This distinction is what later lets you predict which cofactor a given pathway uses.

extra.zh: 老师抱怨的“正反方向不同的酶”是有机制含义的：一对方向相反的通路不能是简单的可逆反应，否则会形成无效循环 (futile cycle) 白白消耗 ATP。所以它们各自有专属的、不可逆的调控步骤——糖酵解的 PFK-1 对糖异生的 FBPase-1，糖原合成的糖原合酶对糖原分解的糖原磷酸化酶——并被互逆调控 (reciprocal regulation)，一个开另一个就关。
extra.en: The "different enzymes in the two directions" the teacher complains about has a mechanistic point: opposing pathways cannot be a single reversible reaction, or they would form a futile cycle burning ATP for nothing. Each therefore owns dedicated irreversible control steps — PFK-1 in glycolysis against FBPase-1 in gluconeogenesis, glycogen synthase against glycogen phosphorylase — under reciprocal regulation, so switching one on switches the other off.

quiz.q_zh: 课上用来定义“一个生命之所以是生命”的标准是？
quiz.q_en: By what criterion does the lecture define a living thing as living?

options.zh: 是否含有任何 DNA
options.en: whether it contains DNA of any kind

options.zh: 是否被膜结构包裹
options.en: whether it is bounded by a membrane

options.zh: 能否进行新陈代谢
options.en: whether it can carry out metabolism

options.zh: 能否自主产生运动
options.en: whether it can move of its own accord

quiz.explain_zh: 课上把新陈代谢——与环境不断进行物质和能量交换——当作生命的定义性特征。自主产生运动这一条连植物和真菌都不满足，含有 DNA 的病毒并不被普遍算作生命，被膜结构包裹也只是形式：脂质体有完整的膜，却没有任何代谢。
quiz.explain_en: The lecture takes metabolism — the continual exchange of matter and energy with the environment — as the defining feature of life. Moving of its own accord fails for plants and fungi, DNA-containing viruses are not generally counted as alive, and being bounded by a membrane is merely a form: a liposome has a complete membrane and no metabolism at all.

quiz.q_zh: 关于合成代谢与分解代谢，下列叙述正确的是？
quiz.q_en: Which statement about anabolism and catabolism is correct?

options.zh: 分解代谢是还原性过程，需要消耗能量
options.en: catabolism is reductive and consumes energy

options.zh: 合成代谢耗能，还原力主要来自 NADPH
options.en: anabolism costs energy and draws on NADPH

options.zh: 合成代谢产能，主要产生还原型 NADH
options.en: anabolism yields energy and produces NADH

options.zh: 分解代谢耗能，还原力主要来自 NADPH
options.en: catabolism costs energy and draws on NADPH

quiz.explain_zh: 合成代谢是耗能的还原性过程，其还原力由 NADPH 提供（如脂肪酸、胆固醇合成）。产能并生成 NADH/FADH2 的是分解代谢，它是氧化性的，把大分子降解为小分子并释放自由能。
quiz.explain_en: Anabolism is a reductive, energy-consuming process whose reducing power comes from NADPH, as in fatty-acid and cholesterol synthesis. It is catabolism that releases energy and generates NADH/FADH2; it is oxidative, breaking large molecules into small ones and liberating free energy.

quiz.q_zh: 在糖酵解和糖异生中，下列哪一步的正、反方向由两种不同的酶催化？
quiz.q_en: Which step is catalysed by two different enzymes in the glycolytic and gluconeogenic directions?

options.zh: 果糖-6-磷酸 ⇄ 果糖-1,6-二磷酸
options.en: fructose-6-P ⇄ fructose-1,6-bisphosphate

options.zh: 3-磷酸甘油醛 ⇄ 磷酸二羟丙酮 DHAP
options.en: glyceraldehyde-3-P ⇄ dihydroxyacetone-P

options.zh: 果糖-1,6-二磷酸 ⇄ 两分子丙糖磷酸
options.en: fructose-1,6-bisP ⇄ two triose phosphates

options.zh: 2-磷酸甘油酸 ⇄ 磷酸烯醇丙酮酸 PEP
options.en: 2-phosphoglycerate ⇄ phosphoenolpyruvate

quiz.explain_zh: 正向由 PFK-1 消耗 ATP 磷酸化，逆向由 FBPase-1 水解磷酸基，是两个不同的酶，也是糖酵解与糖异生之间最重要的互逆调控点。3-磷酸甘油醛与磷酸二羟丙酮之间由丙糖磷酸异构酶催化，果糖-1,6-二磷酸裂解成两分子丙糖磷酸由醛缩酶催化，2-磷酸甘油酸与 PEP 之间由烯醇化酶催化，三者都是近平衡的可逆反应，两个方向用的是同一个酶。
quiz.explain_en: The forward step is an ATP-consuming phosphorylation by PFK-1 and the reverse a hydrolysis by FBPase-1 — two distinct enzymes, and the most important reciprocally regulated point between glycolysis and gluconeogenesis. Triose-phosphate isomerase handles glyceraldehyde-3-P and dihydroxyacetone-P, aldolase splits fructose-1,6-bisphosphate into two triose phosphates, and enolase links 2-phosphoglycerate with PEP; all three are near-equilibrium reversible reactions run by one and the same enzyme in either direction.

title_zh: 供能物质的动员顺序（血糖→糖原→肌肉蛋白→脂肪）与分解代谢的能量去向
title_en: The order in which fuels are mobilised (blood glucose → glycogen → muscle protein → fat) and where catabolic energy actually goes

points.zh: 学生问“体内所有 ATP 是不是都来自糖”，老师说不能这么讲：脂肪可以供能，蛋白质也可以供能；课上给出的说法是人体 ATP 来源“90% 都是糖”；他补充说更可靠的讲法是：ATP 都来自 ATP 合酶以及作为其前提的氢离子（质子梯度），而不是某一种营养物——“ATP 都来源于哪”本来就没有定论，大家一般不这样说
points.en: Asked whether all the body's ATP comes from carbohydrate, the teacher says it cannot be put that way — fat can supply energy and so can protein; the figure he gives in class is that 90% of the body's ATP comes from sugar. He adds that the more defensible statement is that ATP comes from ATP synthase and the protons driving it rather than from any one nutrient, since there is no settled answer to where all ATP comes from and people do not usually put it that way.

points.zh: 饥饿时人体最先消耗的是游离的葡萄糖，也就是吃完饭后游离在血液中的血糖
points.en: On starvation the body first consumes free glucose — the blood sugar circulating after a meal.

points.zh: 血糖消耗完以后开始动用糖原 (glycogen)，包括肝糖原和肌糖原
points.en: Once blood glucose is used up, glycogen is mobilised — both liver glycogen and muscle glycogen.

points.zh: 肌糖原的本职是供无氧运动那种短时间的能量爆发；但即使一动不动躺在床上，呼吸、膈肌也在耗能，当血糖没了、肝糖原已经分解掉 80% 时，就会开始动用肌糖原
points.en: Muscle glycogen's proper job is short bursts of anaerobic exercise; but even lying motionless in bed you keep breathing and your diaphragm keeps spending energy, so once blood glucose is gone and about 80% of liver glycogen has been broken down, muscle glycogen starts to be drawn on.

points.zh: 肌糖原消耗得比较多以后，肌肉就开始分解、蛋白质开始供能——这些都发生在脂肪供能之前
points.en: When muscle glycogen has been substantially depleted, muscle begins to break down and protein starts supplying energy — all of this happening before fat does.

points.zh: 脂肪是最终储藏能源，要到“快死了、再不分解脂肪就活不下去”的程度，才会被积极调动起来
points.en: Fat is the final energy store, mobilised in earnest only when things reach the point of not surviving otherwise.

points.zh: 推论到减肥：光靠饿，最先掉的是水（体内糖分少了跟着脱水，造成体重快速下降的假象），然后掉肌肉，最后才掉脂肪——所以控制饮食加运动才是关键
points.en: Applied to dieting: starving alone loses water first (as carbohydrate stores fall, water goes with them, giving the illusion of rapid weight loss), then muscle, and only last fat — so diet control plus exercise is what matters.

points.zh: 分解代谢中大有机物降解为小的中间产物一定产生能量，但其中 90% 以上以热量形式散失，主要用于维持恒温——这是能量最主要的去向，也是个反常识的点；真正只有大约 5% 被 ATP 或 NADH、FADH、NADPH 这些还原当量所承担
points.en: Breaking large organic molecules down to small intermediates always releases energy, but over 90% of it is lost as heat, mainly to keep the body at constant temperature — the main destination of the energy, and a counter-intuitive point; only about 5% is actually captured by ATP or by reducing equivalents such as NADH, FADH and NADPH.

points.zh: 维生素 B2 对应的 FADH 和维生素 B3（维生素 PP）对应的 NADH 都是氢的载体，这些氢最终在 ATP 合酶那里生成 ATP，所以它们也被称为能量的载体
points.en: The FADH derived from vitamin B2 and the NADH derived from vitamin B3 (vitamin PP) are carriers of hydrogen, and that hydrogen ultimately makes ATP at ATP synthase — which is why they too are called energy carriers.

extra.zh: 「人体内的 ATP 来源有 90% 都是糖」是个很宽泛的说法，实际比例随营养状态大幅移动，与其记这个数字不如记住这层关系：饱食态以葡萄糖为主要燃料（胰岛素高，脂解被抑制）；静息状态和长时间禁食时脂肪酸、酮体成为主要燃料，大脑在长期饥饿中也大量改用酮体；蛋白质只在饥饿后期或糖异生需要碳骨架时才被大量动员。换句话说，燃料在糖和脂肪之间切换，占比不是一个固定数。
extra.en: "90% of the body's ATP comes from carbohydrate" is a loose claim; the real share shifts a great deal with nutritional state, so learn the relationship rather than the number. In the fed state glucose dominates (insulin is high and lipolysis suppressed); at rest and in prolonged fasting fatty acids and ketone bodies dominate, and in long starvation even the brain switches largely to ketones; protein is mobilised heavily only late in fasting or when gluconeogenesis needs carbon skeletons. The fuel mix moves between carbohydrate and fat — it is not a fixed percentage.

extra.zh: 「只有约 5% 被 ATP 承担」这个数偏低。“大部分变成热、少部分被捕获”这个方向是对的，但葡萄糖完全氧化释放的自由能中，被保存进 ATP 高能磷酸键的大约在三分之一的量级（细胞条件下更接近这个区间的上端），其余以热散失。整体食物能量转化为机械功的效率则更低，约四分之一，因为 ATP 用于做功时还要再损失一次。答题时说“多数以热散失、约三分之一被 ATP 保存”比说 5% 稳妥。
extra.en: The "only about 5% captured as ATP" figure is too low. The direction — most becomes heat, a minority is captured — is right, but of the free energy released by completely oxidising glucose, roughly a third is conserved in the high-energy phosphate bonds of ATP (nearer the top of that range under cellular conditions), the rest escaping as heat. Whole-body conversion of food energy into mechanical work is lower still, around a quarter, because using the ATP loses energy a second time. "Most is lost as heat, roughly a third is conserved in ATP" is a safer exam answer than 5%.

extra.zh: 老师把 NADH、FADH2 和 NADPH 并列为“能量载体”，但三者分工不同：NADH 和 FADH2 由分解代谢产生，把电子送进电子传递链去产 ATP；NADPH 主要供还原性生物合成（脂肪酸、胆固醇合成）和抗氧化防御（还原谷胱甘肽），一般不用于产 ATP，其主要来源是磷酸戊糖途径。另外来源要对上：FAD/FMN 来自维生素 B2（核黄素），NAD/NADP 来自维生素 B3（烟酸、维生素 PP）。
extra.en: The lecture lists NADH, FADH2 and NADPH together as energy carriers, but their jobs differ: NADH and FADH2 come from catabolism and deliver electrons to the respiratory chain to make ATP, whereas NADPH mainly serves reductive biosynthesis (fatty acids, cholesterol) and antioxidant defence (regenerating glutathione), is not normally used to make ATP, and comes chiefly from the pentose phosphate pathway. Also keep the vitamins straight: FAD/FMN derive from vitamin B2 (riboflavin), NAD/NADP from vitamin B3 (niacin, vitamin PP).

extra.zh: 写法和机制两点要精确：还原型是 FADH2（两个氢），不是 FADH。而且 NADH 并不是“直接把氢离子交给 ATP 合酶”——它交出的是氢负离子 (hydride，2e⁻ + H⁺)，电子沿电子传递链传递，同时复合体把质子泵到膜间隙形成质子梯度，是这个梯度回流通过 ATP 合酶才生成 ATP，即化学渗透学说 (chemiosmosis)。
extra.en: Two details to get exact: the reduced form is FADH2 (two hydrogens), not FADH. And NADH does not hand protons straight to ATP synthase — it donates a hydride (2e⁻ + H⁺), the electrons travel down the respiratory chain while the complexes pump protons into the intermembrane space, and it is the return flow of that proton gradient through ATP synthase that makes ATP: chemiosmosis.

quiz.q_zh: 按课上讲的顺序，人在持续饥饿时动员供能物质的先后是？
quiz.q_en: In the order given in the lecture, how does the body mobilise fuels during continued starvation?

options.zh: 血糖 → 糖原 → 肌肉蛋白 → 脂肪
options.en: blood glucose → glycogen → muscle protein → fat

options.zh: 脂肪 → 血糖 → 糖原 → 肌肉蛋白
options.en: fat → blood glucose → glycogen → muscle protein

options.zh: 糖原 → 脂肪 → 血糖 → 肌肉蛋白
options.en: glycogen → fat → blood glucose → muscle protein

options.zh: 肌肉蛋白 → 血糖 → 糖原 → 脂肪
options.en: muscle protein → blood glucose → glycogen → fat

quiz.explain_zh: 先用血液中的游离葡萄糖，再动用肝糖原和肌糖原，糖原大量消耗后肌肉开始分解蛋白质供能，脂肪作为最终储备最后才被积极调动。把脂肪或肌肉蛋白排在最前面，正好和课上强调的“减肥先掉水、再掉肌肉、最后掉脂肪”相反。
quiz.explain_en: Free glucose in the blood goes first, then liver and muscle glycogen; once glycogen is well depleted muscle protein starts contributing, and fat, the final reserve, is mobilised in earnest last. Putting fat or muscle protein first contradicts the lecture's point that dieting loses water, then muscle, and only then fat.

quiz.q_zh: 分解代谢释放出的能量，其最主要的去向是？
quiz.q_en: Where does most of the energy released by catabolism actually go?

options.zh: 以热量形式散失，用来维持体温
options.en: lost as heat, which maintains body temperature

options.zh: 全部保存在 ATP 的高能键中
options.en: conserved entirely in ATP's high-energy bonds

options.zh: 转变为 NADPH 供还原性合成
options.en: converted into NADPH for reductive biosynthesis

options.zh: 直接储存成糖原和脂肪等储备
options.en: stored directly as glycogen and fat reserves

quiz.explain_zh: 大部分自由能以热的形式散失，恒温动物正是靠它维持体温，只有一部分被 ATP 和还原当量捕获——这是课上强调的“反常识”之处。能量不可能全部保存进 ATP（那需要 100% 的效率），NADPH 主要来自磷酸戊糖途径而不是分解代谢释放能量的主流去向，糖原和脂肪则是合成代谢的产物，属于物质储备而非能量去向。
quiz.explain_en: Most of the free energy escapes as heat, which is exactly how a warm-blooded animal holds its temperature, and only part is captured as ATP and reducing equivalents — the counter-intuitive point the lecture stresses. It cannot all be conserved in ATP (that would demand 100% efficiency), NADPH comes chiefly from the pentose phosphate pathway rather than being the main destination here, and glycogen and fat are anabolic products — material stores, not a destination for the energy catabolism releases.

quiz.q_zh: 关于 NADH 与 NADPH，下列叙述正确的是？
quiz.q_en: Which statement about NADH and NADPH is correct?

options.zh: NADH 和 NADPH 都由维生素 B2 衍生
options.en: NADH and NADPH derive alike from vitamin B2 riboflavin

options.zh: NADH 主要进入电子传递链，用于生成 ATP
options.en: NADH mainly feeds the respiratory chain to make ATP

options.zh: NADPH 主要进入电子传递链，用于生成 ATP
options.en: NADPH mainly feeds the respiratory chain to make ATP

options.zh: NADH 和 NADPH 都主要用于还原性合成
options.en: NADH and NADPH serve mainly in reductive biosynthesis

quiz.explain_zh: NADH 由分解代谢产生，把电子送进电子传递链用于产 ATP；NADPH 则主要供脂肪酸、胆固醇等还原性合成和谷胱甘肽抗氧化，主要来自磷酸戊糖途径，不走产 ATP 的路，因此 NADH 与 NADPH 的去向并不相同。NADH 与 NADPH 的骨架都来自维生素 B3（烟酸、维生素 PP），来自维生素 B2 核黄素的是 FAD 和 FMN。
quiz.explain_en: NADH is generated by catabolism and delivers electrons to the respiratory chain for ATP synthesis, whereas NADPH serves reductive syntheses such as fatty acids and cholesterol plus glutathione-based antioxidant defence, comes largely from the pentose phosphate pathway, and never takes the ATP-producing route — so the two do not share a destination. The skeletons of NADH and NADPH alike derive from vitamin B3 (niacin, vitamin PP); it is FAD and FMN that come from riboflavin, vitamin B2.

title_zh: 分解代谢/合成代谢收尾与ATP作为能量通货
title_en: Catabolism/Anabolism Wrap-up and ATP as the Energy Currency

points.zh: 分解代谢释放的能量中，绝大部分（90%以上，讲课后段又给出95%）以热量形式散失，主要用于维持体温；只有约5%被ATP或还原当量（NADH、FADH2、NADPH）承载。
points.en: Most of the energy released by catabolism (over 90%, later restated as 95%) is lost as heat used to maintain body temperature; only about 5% is captured by ATP or reducing equivalents (NADH, FADH2, NADPH).

points.zh: 合成代谢(anabolism)是分解代谢的逆过程：用能量把小分子聚合成大分子有机物。
points.en: Anabolism is the reverse of catabolism: it uses energy to build large organic molecules from small ones.

points.zh: 生物分为自养生物(autotroph)和异养生物(heterotroph)：狭义自养生物是以CO2作为唯一碳源构建所有含碳分子的生物，包括植物及一部分分解者细菌；异养生物必须从环境中获取复杂有机分子作为原料。
points.en: Organisms are classified as autotrophs or heterotrophs: an autotroph (narrow sense) builds all its carbon compounds using CO2 as the sole carbon source — this includes plants and some decomposer bacteria; a heterotroph must obtain complex organic molecules from the environment.

points.zh: 人体内ATP、GTP、UTP、CTP都能供能，但用量最多的是ATP；ATP主要起能量传递(energy transfer)的作用。
points.en: In the human body ATP, GTP, UTP and CTP can all supply energy, but ATP is used the most; ATP's main role is energy transfer.

points.zh: ATP的能量储存是短暂的：ATP处于快速消耗与快速再生的动态平衡中，不是先合成存起来、需要时再用，而是边合成边消耗，在需要的位点发挥功能。
points.en: ATP storage is transient: ATP exists in a dynamic steady state of rapid consumption and regeneration — it is not synthesized and stockpiled for later use, but made and used continuously right where it is needed.

points.zh: ATP的三个磷酸基团从核糖端数起依次是α、β、γ磷酸；γ磷酸键是高能磷酸键，不稳定，容易断开。
points.en: ATP's three phosphate groups, counting from the ribose, are α, β and γ; the γ-phosphate bond is the high-energy bond and is unstable, easily broken.

extra.zh: 讲课先说"90%以上"（01:55段）后说"95%"（02:07段）以热能散失，这是数量级近似值，不同教材因所选代谢反应不同会给出略有差异的具体百分比，但"大部分自由能转化为热能、只有小部分被ATP等载体捕获"这个定性结论是稳定的。
extra.en: The lecture gives "over 90%" (around 01:55) and later "95%" (around 02:07) for the heat-loss fraction — these are order-of-magnitude approximations that vary slightly by textbook and reaction, but the qualitative point (most free energy becomes heat, only a small fraction is captured as ATP) is robust.

extra.zh: 自养/异养的分类还可细分为光能自养(photoautotroph)和化能自养(chemoautotroph)，讲课给出的"以CO2为唯一碳源"是这一分类考试中的基础定义。
extra.en: Autotroph/heterotroph classification can be further split into photoautotrophs and chemoautotrophs; the "CO2 as sole carbon source" definition given in lecture is the exam-level baseline for this classification.

extra.zh: NADH/FADH2/NADPH作为还原当量最终把电子交给电子传递链(electron transport chain)，驱动质子梯度使ATP合酶产生ATP，这条机制链条讲课这里没有展开，会在后续氧化磷酸化内容中讲到。
extra.en: NADH/FADH2/NADPH as reducing equivalents ultimately feed electrons into the electron transport chain, driving the proton gradient that ATP synthase uses to make ATP — this mechanistic chain wasn't elaborated here and will come with oxidative phosphorylation.

extra.zh: NADH主要参与分解代谢产能反应，NADPH结构上只多一个2'-磷酸基团，却主要用于合成代谢的还原反应（如脂肪酸合成）；两者角色不可互换，考试中常被混淆。
extra.en: NADH mainly participates in catabolic energy-producing reactions, while NADPH — structurally just one 2'-phosphate different — is mainly used for reductive biosynthesis (e.g. fatty acid synthesis); the two roles are not interchangeable and are commonly confused on exams.

quiz.q_zh: 关于人体分解代谢释放的能量去向，下列说法正确的是？
quiz.q_en: Regarding where the energy released by catabolism in the human body goes, which statement is correct?

options.zh: 绝大部分直接转化为ATP，只小部分以热能散失
options.en: mostly converted straight into ATP, a little lost as heat

options.zh: 能量大致对半分给散热和ATP捕获，比例相当
options.en: divided about half and half between heat and ATP capture

options.zh: 几乎全部能量都储存进ATP，几乎不产生热能
options.en: almost all of it stored in ATP, with almost no heat made

options.zh: 绝大部分变成热能维持体温，小部分被ATP捕获
options.en: mostly heat keeping body temperature, some caught by ATP

quiz.explain_zh: 讲课明确说 90% 以上、接近 95% 的能量以热量形式散失，只有约 5% 被 ATP 或 NADH/FADH2/NADPH 等还原当量载体承担，因此既不是绝大部分直接进 ATP，也不是散热与 ATP 捕获大致对半，更不可能几乎全部存进 ATP 而不产热——那等于要求代谢的能量转换效率接近 100%。
quiz.explain_en: The lecture states that over 90%, close to 95%, of the energy is lost as heat and only about 5% is carried by ATP or reducing-equivalent carriers such as NADH/FADH2/NADPH. So it is neither mostly routed straight into ATP nor split evenly between heat and ATP, and certainly not stored almost entirely in ATP with no heat — that would demand an energy-conversion efficiency near 100%.

quiz.q_zh: 关于"自养生物"(autotroph，狭义定义)，下列哪项说法正确？
quiz.q_en: Regarding the narrow-sense definition of "autotroph", which statement is correct?

options.zh: 必须在持续光照条件下才能进行任何代谢活动的生物
options.en: An organism that can carry out metabolic activity only under continuous illumination by light

options.zh: 只存在于绿色植物中、在细菌中完全不存在的生物
options.en: An organism found only among green plants and entirely absent from every bacterial species

options.zh: 能以CO2作为唯一碳源合成所有含碳分子的生物
options.en: An organism that builds every carbon-containing molecule from CO2 as its sole carbon source

options.zh: 只能利用现成有机分子中的碳来构筑自身细胞的生物
options.en: An organism that can only use carbon from ready-made organic molecules to build its own cells

quiz.explain_zh: 讲课定义自养生物(狭义)是以二氧化碳作为唯一碳源构建所有含碳分子的生物。靠现成有机分子取碳的是异养生物；自养并不要求光照，硝化细菌等化能自养细菌在黑暗中即可固定CO2；自养也不限于绿色植物，细菌中同样存在。
quiz.explain_en: Lecture defines the narrow-sense autotroph as an organism that uses CO2 as its sole carbon source to build all carbon-containing molecules. Taking carbon from ready-made organic molecules is what defines a heterotroph; light is not required, since chemoautotrophs such as nitrifying bacteria fix CO2 in the dark; and autotrophy is not restricted to green plants, as bacteria show it too.

quiz.q_zh: 关于ATP在人体内的储存和使用方式，下列描述最准确的是？
quiz.q_en: Which description of how ATP is stored and used in the body is most accurate?

options.zh: ATP处于快速消耗和快速再生的动态平衡，边产生边消耗
options.en: ATP sits in a dynamic steady state of rapid consumption and regeneration, made and used continuously

options.zh: ATP一旦合成就被稳定储存起来，直到细胞需要时才被动用
options.en: Once synthesized, ATP is stably stockpiled in the cell and drawn on only when the cell later needs it

options.zh: ATP只在需要能量的细胞器内被合成，合成之后不会移动
options.en: ATP is synthesized only inside the organelle that needs it and never moves elsewhere afterwards

options.zh: ATP的浓度随代谢状态大幅波动，始终没有稳定的区间
options.en: ATP concentration swings widely with the metabolic state and never settles into any stable range

quiz.explain_zh: 讲课强调ATP并不是先攒起来再用，而是不断地边消耗边再生，处于动态平衡：它不会被稳定囤积等待动用；它可以自由扩散离开合成位置去供能，并不困在某个细胞器内；人体内ATP浓度总体维持在比较恒定的区间，而不是大幅波动。
quiz.explain_en: The lecture stresses that ATP is not stockpiled for later use but is continuously consumed and regenerated in a dynamic steady state. It is not held in a stable reserve awaiting use; it diffuses away from where it was made rather than staying inside one organelle; and the body's overall ATP level is kept fairly constant instead of swinging widely.

title_zh: GPCR信号转导与NAD/FAD的氢原子传递化学
title_en: GPCR Signal Transduction and NAD/FAD Hydrogen-Carrier Chemistry

points.zh: GTP除了供能，还参与G蛋白偶联受体(GPCR, G protein-coupled receptor)的信号转导，是ATP之外相对重要的核苷三磷酸。
points.en: Besides supplying energy, GTP participates in signal transduction at G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) — among the non-ATP nucleoside triphosphates, GTP is relatively important.

points.zh: GPCR中的"G"指的是与受体偶联的G蛋白，它利用GTP的水解进行信号转化，GTP在提供信号的同时也提供能量给受体。
points.en: The "G" in GPCR refers to the G protein coupled to the receptor; it uses GTP hydrolysis to transduce the signal, so GTP supplies both a signal and energy.

points.zh: CTP、UTP的重要性远低于ATP/GTP：CTP不太重要，UTP主要只在RNA代谢途径中产生和使用，用量更少。
points.en: CTP and UTP matter far less than ATP/GTP: CTP is not very important, and UTP is mainly produced and used within the RNA metabolic pathway, so it is used even less.

points.zh: NAD（讲课把维生素PP、烟酰胺、维生素B3当作同一个概念）作为辅酶(coenzyme)，其烟酰胺(nicotinamide)部分可以接受1个氢原子。
points.en: NAD — lecture treats vitamin PP, nicotinamide and vitamin B3 as the same concept — acts as a coenzyme whose nicotinamide portion can accept one hydrogen atom.

points.zh: FAD/FMN（维生素B2的衍生物）可以同时接受2个氢原子，因为其环上有两个氮原子分别可以各结合一个氢质子。
points.en: FAD/FMN (derivatives of vitamin B2) can accept two hydrogens at once, because two nitrogen atoms on the ring can each bind one proton.

points.zh: 讲课认为NAD和FAD在生化中功能相似——都负责转移氢质子——区别主要在于一次转移的氢原子数目（1个 vs 2个），在不同氧化环节各自发挥作用。
points.en: The lecture treats NAD and FAD as functionally similar — both transfer hydrogen — differing mainly in how many hydrogens each carries at once (one vs. two), acting at different oxidation steps.

points.zh: 这些氢载体都属于辅酶(coenzyme)：单独存在时没有催化活性，必须结合到酶上才能一起发挥催化功能。
points.en: These hydrogen carriers are all coenzymes: alone they have no catalytic activity; they must bind to an enzyme to function catalytically.

extra.zh: NAD+实际接受的是一个氢负离子(hydride, H-，携带2个电子)，另一个质子留在溶液中，标准写法是NAD+ + 2H+ + 2e- → NADH + H+，比课堂"接受一个氢原子"的说法更精确，是常考细节。
extra.en: NAD+ actually accepts a hydride ion (H-, carrying 2 electrons), with the other proton released into solution; the standard notation is NAD+ + 2H+ + 2e- → NADH + H+, more precise than the lecture's "accepts one hydrogen atom" and a common exam detail.

extra.zh: NAD(H)主要用于分解代谢产能反应，NADP(H)只多一个2'-磷酸基团，却主要用于合成代谢的还原反应（如脂肪酸、胆固醇合成），二者不能互换使用。
extra.en: NAD(H) is mainly used in catabolic energy-producing reactions, while NADP(H) — differing by only a 2'-phosphate group — is mainly used in reductive biosynthesis (e.g. fatty acid, cholesterol synthesis); the two are not interchangeable.

extra.zh: GPCR下游的经典机制——配体结合后GDP-GTP交换、Gα亚基激活腺苷酸环化酶产生cAMP等第二信使——讲课只提到GTP参与信号转化，没有展开具体级联。
extra.en: The classic GPCR downstream cascade — ligand binding triggers GDP-GTP exchange, the Gα subunit activates adenylate cyclase to produce cAMP — was not elaborated; lecture only mentions that GTP participates in signal transduction.

extra.zh: FAD (flavin adenine dinucleotide) 比FMN (flavin mononucleotide) 多一个AMP基团，两者的黄素环化学性质相同，都能携带2个氢原子/2个电子。
extra.en: FAD (flavin adenine dinucleotide) has an extra AMP group compared to FMN (flavin mononucleotide); their flavin rings are chemically identical and both carry 2 hydrogens/2 electrons.

quiz.q_zh: 关于NAD和FAD携带氢原子（还原当量）的能力，下列说法正确的是？
quiz.q_en: Regarding the hydrogen-carrying (reducing-equivalent) capacity of NAD and FAD, which statement is correct?

options.zh: NAD和FAD在一次氧化还原反应中都只能接受1个氢原子
options.en: Both NAD and FAD can accept only 1 hydrogen atom in any single redox reaction

options.zh: NAD和FAD在一次氧化还原反应中都能接受2个氢原子
options.en: Both NAD and FAD can accept 2 hydrogen atoms at once in a single redox reaction

options.zh: NAD一次可接受1个氢原子，FAD一次可接受2个氢原子
options.en: NAD can accept 1 hydrogen at a time, while FAD can accept 2 hydrogens at a time

options.zh: NAD一次可接受2个氢原子，FAD一次可接受1个氢原子
options.en: NAD can accept 2 hydrogens at a time, while FAD can accept 1 hydrogen at a time

quiz.explain_zh: 讲课明确说明NAD（烟酰胺部分）一次只能接受1个氢原子，而FAD/FMN环上有两个可结合质子的氮原子，能同时接受2个氢原子。因此把两者的容量对调、把两者都限成1个、或把两者都算成2个，都与烟酰胺环和异咯嗪环的化学结构不符。
quiz.explain_en: The lecture explains that NAD (via its nicotinamide portion) accepts only one hydrogen at a time, while FAD/FMN has two ring nitrogens that can each bind a proton, accepting two hydrogens at once. Swapping the two capacities, limiting both to one, or crediting both with two all contradict the chemistry of the nicotinamide and isoalloxazine rings.

quiz.q_zh: 关于GPCR (G protein-coupled receptor) 中GTP的作用，下列描述正确的是？
quiz.q_en: Regarding the role of GTP in GPCR (G protein-coupled receptor) signaling, which description is correct?

options.zh: GPCR的信号转导完全不依赖任何核苷三磷酸分子
options.en: GPCR signal transduction proceeds without any nucleoside triphosphate being involved at all

options.zh: GTP参与G蛋白的信号转化，同时也为受体提供能量
options.en: GTP takes part in the G protein's signal transduction and also supplies energy to the receptor

options.zh: GTP只为受体提供能量，完全不参与信号的转导过程
options.en: GTP serves purely as an energy source for the receptor and plays no part at all in transduction

options.zh: GPCR信号转导中G蛋白使用UTP而不是GTP
options.en: In GPCR signal transduction the G protein uses UTP instead of GTP to relay the signal onward

quiz.explain_zh: 讲课说明GPCR里的G蛋白利用GTP进行信号转化，GTP在提供信号的同时也提供能量给G蛋白偶联受体。说GTP只供能不传信号，抹掉了Gα结合GTP作为开关的核心作用；G蛋白结合的核苷酸是GTP而非UTP；整个通路也确实依赖核苷三磷酸。
quiz.explain_en: The lecture explains that the G protein in a GPCR uses GTP to transduce the signal, so GTP supplies both a signal and energy to the receptor. Calling GTP a pure energy source erases the switch role of GTP-bound Gα; the nucleotide the G protein binds is GTP, not UTP; and the pathway does depend on a nucleoside triphosphate.

quiz.q_zh: 下列哪种核苷三磷酸在讲课中被描述为"主要只在RNA代谢途径中产生"，因而用量最少？
quiz.q_en: Which nucleoside triphosphate does the lecture describe as "mainly produced only within the RNA metabolic pathway", making it the least used?

options.zh: GTP
options.en: GTP

options.zh: CTP
options.en: CTP

options.zh: ATP
options.en: ATP

options.zh: UTP
options.en: UTP

quiz.explain_zh: 讲课特别指出UTP只有在RNA的代谢途径里才会产生，所以除了ATP和GTP，UTP用得都很少，比CTP更少见。ATP是通用能量货币，GTP用于GPCR信号转导和蛋白质合成，CTP在磷脂合成中也有专门用途。
quiz.explain_en: The lecture specifically notes that UTP is only produced within the RNA metabolic pathway, so aside from ATP and GTP it is used even less than CTP. ATP is the universal energy currency, GTP drives GPCR signaling and protein synthesis, and CTP has its own dedicated role in phospholipid synthesis.

title_zh: 泛酸与辅酶A、乙酰基团运输，及新陈代谢的分层调节
title_en: Pantothenic Acid, Coenzyme A, Acetyl-Group Transport, and Levels of Metabolic Regulation

points.zh: 泛酸(pantothenic acid, 维生素B5)是辅酶A(CoA, coenzyme A / "SCoA")的组成部分之一。
points.en: Pantothenic acid (vitamin B5) is a structural component of coenzyme A (CoA / "SCoA").

points.zh: 乙酰辅酶A(acetyl-CoA)中乙酰基团与CoA之间的键是高能硫酯键(high-energy thioester bond)，讲课把它归入高能键一并讨论。
points.en: In acetyl-CoA, the bond linking the acetyl group to CoA is a high-energy thioester bond, which the lecture discusses together with the other high-energy bonds.

points.zh: CoA的主要功能是运输二碳单位(2-carbon unit)，即乙酰基团(acetyl group)，这一点会在糖酵解(glycolysis)和脂肪酸代谢(fatty acid metabolism)中详细讲到。
points.en: CoA's main function is to shuttle two-carbon units — acetyl groups — a role that will be elaborated on in glycolysis and fatty-acid metabolism.

points.zh: 代谢研究方法（同位素法、气体测定法、酶抑制法等）现在实际使用较少，同位素法(isotope labeling)相对用得还多一些。
points.en: Classic metabolic research methods (isotope labeling, gas measurement, enzyme-inhibition studies) are rarely used today; isotope labeling is used comparatively more than the others.

points.zh: 新陈代谢的调节分三个层级：分子水平（酶和底物浓度的调节，如抑制剂、底物浓度、酶的变构调节allosteric regulation）。
points.en: Metabolic regulation occurs at three levels: the molecular level (regulation of enzyme and substrate concentration — inhibitors, substrate concentration, allosteric regulation).

points.zh: 细胞水平的调节（讲课称为人体最主要的代谢调节方式）：细胞通过特殊结构实现酶活性的空间分隔控制(compartmentalization)。
points.en: Cellular-level regulation — described in lecture as the body's dominant mode of metabolic control — uses special structures to spatially compartmentalize enzyme activity.

points.zh: 课堂举例：耗能多的肌肉细胞里，产ATP的ATP合酶更靠近肌动蛋白/肌球蛋白等做功蛋白；讲课称内脏器官细胞里ATP合酶可能更靠近核糖体或内质网，因为这些细胞的ATP主要用于合成代谢。
points.en: Lecture's example: in energy-hungry muscle cells, ATP synthase is said to sit closer to actin/myosin; the lecture states that in visceral-organ cells, ATP synthase may sit closer to ribosomes or the ER, because those cells' ATP is used mainly for biosynthesis.

points.zh: 整体水平（有机体水平）的调节是激素与神经的调节，作用于器官/组织层面。
points.en: Whole-organism-level regulation is hormonal and neural regulation, acting at the organ/tissue level.

extra.zh: "内脏器官细胞里ATP合酶更靠近核糖体/内质网，因为这些细胞需要ATP用于蛋白质合成"不是标准生物学说法。线粒体ATP合酶的密度主要取决于细胞整体的呼吸/能量需求和嵴(cristae)表面积，而不是与内质网的物理距离；ATP本身能自由扩散于细胞质中到达任何需要它的地方，这正是它作为"通用能量货币"而不是"就地按需合成"的意义所在（约02:05:27-02:05:59）。
extra.en: "ATP synthase sits closer to ribosomes/ER in visceral cells because those cells need ATP for protein synthesis" is not standard biology. Mitochondrial ATP synthase density tracks a cell's overall respiratory demand and cristae surface area, not proximity to the ER — ATP diffuses freely through the cytosol to wherever it is needed, which is the whole point of it being a universal energy currency rather than made on-site per organelle (around 02:05:27-02:05:59).

extra.zh: 高能硫酯键(thioester bond)水解自由能量级与ATP的γ磷酸键相近，这也是二者都被归入"高能键"讨论的化学基础。
extra.en: The free energy of hydrolysis of a thioester bond is on the same order of magnitude as ATP's γ-phosphate bond, which is the chemical basis for discussing both together as "high-energy bonds".

extra.zh: 变构调节(allosteric regulation)是分子水平代谢调节的核心考点，典型例子是别构酶受终产物负反馈抑制(feedback inhibition)，会在代谢通路调控（如糖酵解中的磷酸果糖激酶-1）中反复出现。
extra.en: Allosteric regulation is a core exam topic at the molecular level, typified by allosteric enzymes under end-product feedback inhibition — it recurs in pathway control examples such as phosphofructokinase-1 in glycolysis.

extra.zh: 辅酶(coenzyme，如CoA、NAD)与辅基(prosthetic group，多数FAD属于此类，与酶紧密甚至共价结合)是有区别的：辅酶通常可逆结合、可解离，辅基则不易解离；讲课把NAD/FAD/CoA都笼统称为"辅酶"未做这一区分。
extra.en: Coenzymes (e.g. CoA, NAD) differ from prosthetic groups (FAD is usually this type, tightly or covalently bound to the enzyme): coenzymes typically bind reversibly and can dissociate, prosthetic groups do not; the lecture lumps NAD/FAD/CoA together as "coenzymes" without this distinction.

quiz.q_zh: 关于细胞水平代谢调节中"特殊结构实现酶活性的空间分隔控制"，下列哪项是标准生物学观点？
quiz.q_en: Regarding cellular-level metabolic regulation via "special structures compartmentalizing enzyme activity", which is the standard biological view?

options.zh: 分泌旺盛的细胞会把ATP合酶特意定位到内质网旁以直接供能
options.en: In secretory cells ATP synthase is deliberately positioned beside the ER to power protein synthesis

options.zh: 所有细胞的ATP合酶分布是完全均一的，不存在细胞类型差异
options.en: ATP synthase distribution is completely uniform in every cell, with no differences between cell types

options.zh: ATP合酶的密度只由激素水平决定，与细胞的呼吸需求无关
options.en: ATP synthase density is fixed by hormone levels alone, unrelated to the cell's respiratory demand

options.zh: 线粒体ATP合酶的密度主要取决于细胞整体的呼吸与能量需求
options.en: Mitochondrial ATP synthase density mainly tracks the cell's overall respiratory and energy demand

quiz.explain_zh: 标准观点是线粒体ATP合酶密度/嵴表面积与细胞整体呼吸需求相关。ATP作为通用能量货币可自由扩散到需要它的位置，不会因内质网"需要ATP"就把ATP合酶特意定位到旁边；心肌与皮肤成纤维细胞的线粒体含量差别巨大，说明分布并非各细胞均一；激素可以影响线粒体生成，但决定密度的仍是细胞自身的呼吸需求。
quiz.explain_en: The standard view is that mitochondrial ATP synthase density tracks a cell's overall respiratory demand and cristae area. ATP as a universal energy currency diffuses freely to where it is needed, so the enzyme is not deliberately parked beside the ER; mitochondrial content differs enormously between cardiomyocytes and skin fibroblasts, so the distribution is not uniform across cells; and while hormones can influence mitochondrial biogenesis, what sets the density is the cell's own respiratory demand.

quiz.q_zh: CoA (辅酶A) 在代谢中的核心功能是什么？
quiz.q_en: What is the core function of CoA (coenzyme A) in metabolism?

options.zh: 在DNA复制中作为引物酶合成RNA引物以起始新链的延伸
options.en: Acting as the primase that makes the RNA primers starting new strand synthesis in DNA replication

options.zh: 作为氢原子的载体负责在NAD和FAD之间直接传递还原当量
options.en: Acting as the hydrogen carrier that shuttles reducing equivalents directly between NAD and FAD

options.zh: 运输二碳单位（乙酰基团），在糖酵解和脂肪酸代谢中发挥作用
options.en: Shuttling two-carbon units (acetyl groups), functioning in glycolysis and fatty-acid metabolism

options.zh: 在线粒体电子传递链末端作为最终电子受体接受电子并生成水
options.en: Serving as the terminal electron acceptor at the end of the electron transport chain, forming water

quiz.explain_zh: 讲课明确CoA/SCoA的主要作用是通过硫酯键运输二碳单位（乙酰基团），会在糖酵解和脂肪酸代谢中详细讲到。电子传递链的最终电子受体是氧分子；合成RNA引物的是引物酶(primase)这一蛋白质；氢原子/还原当量由NAD和FAD自身携带，CoA不参与这一传递。
quiz.explain_en: The lecture states that CoA/SCoA's main role is shuttling two-carbon units (acetyl groups) through its thioester bond, a role elaborated later in glycolysis and fatty-acid metabolism. The terminal electron acceptor of the transport chain is molecular oxygen; RNA primers are made by the protein enzyme primase; and reducing equivalents are carried by NAD and FAD themselves, with no role for CoA in that transfer.

quiz.q_zh: 新陈代谢调节的三个层级，按讲课顺序是？
quiz.q_en: In the order presented in lecture, what are the three levels of metabolic regulation?

options.zh: 细胞水平（结构分隔定位）→ 分子水平（酶与底物浓度）→ 整体水平（激素神经调节）
options.en: Cellular (structural compartmentation) -> molecular (enzyme/substrate levels) -> organismal (hormonal/neural)

options.zh: 整体水平（激素神经调节）→ 分子水平（酶与底物浓度）→ 细胞水平（结构分隔定位）
options.en: Organismal (hormonal/neural) -> molecular (enzyme/substrate levels) -> cellular (structural compartmentation)

options.zh: 分子水平（酶与底物浓度）→ 细胞水平（结构分隔定位）→ 整体水平（激素神经调节）
options.en: Molecular (enzyme/substrate levels) -> cellular (structural compartmentation) -> organismal (hormonal/neural)

options.zh: 整体水平（激素神经调节）→ 细胞水平（结构分隔定位）→ 分子水平（酶与底物浓度）
options.en: Organismal (hormonal/neural) -> cellular (structural compartmentation) -> molecular (enzyme/substrate levels)

quiz.explain_zh: 讲课依次由小到大介绍：分子水平（酶/底物浓度、变构调节）→ 细胞水平（人体最主要的调节方式，依靠特殊结构实现空间分隔）→ 整体水平（激素与神经调节）。其余三种排列都把讲课的由小到大顺序打乱了：或从整体讲起，或把细胞水平提到分子水平之前，或把细胞水平放到最后。
quiz.explain_en: The lecture works from small to large: molecular level (enzyme/substrate concentration, allosteric regulation) -> cellular level (the body's dominant mode, via structural compartmentation) -> organismal level (hormonal and neural regulation). The other three orderings break that small-to-large sequence, either starting from the organism, or putting the cellular level ahead of the molecular one, or leaving the cellular level until last.

title_zh: 生物能学导论：封闭系统假设、热力学第一定律与标准自由能变
title_en: Introduction to Bioenergetics: Closed-System Assumptions, the First Law, and Standard Free Energy

points.zh: 整体水平（有机体水平）的代谢调节是激素与神经系统的调节，作用于器官/组织层面；讲课在此简单带过，转入生物能学(bioenergetics)部分。
points.en: Whole-organism-level metabolic regulation is hormonal and neural, acting at the organ/tissue level; lecture passes over this briefly before moving into bioenergetics.

points.zh: 讨论人体内的生物能学时，前提是把人体当作一个等压(isobaric)、等体积(isochoric)、等温(isothermal)的封闭体系。
points.en: Discussing bioenergetics in the human body assumes it is a closed system that is isobaric, isochoric (constant volume), and isothermal.

points.zh: 能量的形式主要分两种：热能(heat)和做功(work)；人体讨论更关注做功，因为约95%的能量以热能形式散失。
points.en: Energy takes two main forms: heat and work; discussion of the body focuses on work, since roughly 95% of energy is lost as heat.

points.zh: 热力学第一定律(first law of thermodynamics)：能量既不能凭空产生也不能凭空消失，只能从一种形式转化为另一种形式。
points.en: The first law of thermodynamics: energy is neither created nor destroyed, only converted between forms.

points.zh: 例如一分子葡萄糖的化学能不会消失，只会转化为约95%散失的热能和约5%储存为ATP的能量，这是生化里讨论生物能学的例子。
points.en: For example, the chemical energy of one glucose molecule does not vanish — it converts into roughly 95% lost heat and roughly 5% stored as ATP, the example lecture uses for bioenergetics.

points.zh: 标准生化自由能变(ΔG°′, standard biochemical free energy change)是在pH 7、恒温恒压恒体积等生理相关条件下定义的自由能变；讲课说这套公式推导本身不需要记，只需理解定义的意义。
points.en: The standard biochemical free energy change (ΔG°′) is defined under physiologically relevant conditions — pH 7, constant temperature/pressure/volume; lecture says the derivation itself need not be memorized, only the meaning of the definition.

points.zh: 一般自由能变(ΔG)在任何条件下都可计算，数值与pH、温度、浓度相关；经典物理化学的标准自由能变(ΔG°)是在25°C、1大气压、底物浓度1 mol/L、pH = 0的条件下测得。
points.en: The general free energy change (ΔG) can be calculated under any conditions and depends on pH, temperature and concentration; the classical physical-chemistry standard free energy change (ΔG°) is defined at 25°C, 1 atm, 1 mol/L substrate concentration and pH 0.

points.zh: 人体内实际反应条件是37°C、1大气压、pH 7，底物/产物浓度也会变化，因此生化用ΔG°′这套更贴近生理条件的标准来描述人体内的自由能变。
points.en: Actual reactions in the body occur at 37°C, 1 atm, pH 7, with varying substrate/product concentrations, so biochemistry uses ΔG°′, closer to physiological conditions, to describe in vivo free energy changes.

extra.zh: 标准生化条件ΔG°′与经典物理化学标准条件ΔG°的关键差异是pH：物理化学标准态定义在pH 0（[H+] = 1 mol/L），而生化标准态固定在pH = 7（[H+] = 10⁻⁷ mol/L），这个差异对涉及H+的反应影响很大，是ΔG°与ΔG°′之间经常需要换算的原因。
extra.en: The key difference between the standard biochemical condition (ΔG°′) and the classical physical-chemistry condition (ΔG°) is pH: physical chemistry's standard state is pH 0 ([H+] = 1 mol/L), while biochemistry's standard state fixes pH at 7 ([H+] = 10⁻⁷ mol/L); this matters a lot for reactions involving H+, which is why conversion between ΔG° and ΔG°′ is often required.

extra.zh: 吉布斯自由能变的关系式 ΔG = ΔG°′ + RT ln([产物]/[底物]) 把标准自由能变换算成细胞内实际自由能变，讲课说"公式不用看"，但这是判断某反应在体内是否自发的常考公式，建议课后单独补充记忆。
extra.en: The Gibbs free energy relation ΔG = ΔG°′ + RT ln([products]/[substrates]) converts the standard free energy change into the actual in-cell free energy change; the lecture says the formula "needn't be looked at", but it is a common exam formula for judging whether a reaction is spontaneous in vivo, worth memorizing separately.

extra.zh: 热力学第一定律讲的是能量守恒，不涉及能量转化的方向性；能量究竟是变热还是变ATP这种"分配"，实际上由热力学第二定律和自由能变(ΔG)决定，第一定律本身只保证总能量守恒。
extra.en: The first law of thermodynamics concerns energy conservation, not the direction of energy conversion; whether energy becomes heat or ATP is determined by the second law and the free energy change (ΔG) — the first law alone only guarantees total energy is conserved.

extra.zh: "人体是等压等体积等温体系"是生物能学教学中常用的简化假设，实际人体并非严格恒定体积（如呼吸导致的胸腔容积变化），考试中按标准假设处理即可。
extra.en: "The body is isobaric, isochoric and isothermal" is a standard simplifying assumption used in teaching bioenergetics; the real body is not strictly constant-volume (e.g. breathing changes thoracic volume), but exams treat it under the standard assumption.

quiz.q_zh: 关于热力学第一定律在生化中的应用，下列说法正确的是？
quiz.q_en: Regarding the application of the first law of thermodynamics in biochemistry, which statement is correct?

options.zh: 第一定律只适用于开放系统，对人体这样的封闭体系并不成立
options.en: The first law applies only to open systems and fails for a closed system like the body

options.zh: 能量既不会凭空产生也不会消失，只能在不同形式之间相互转化
options.en: Energy is neither created nor destroyed and can only be converted among different forms

options.zh: 生物体内的能量总是自发地从热能转化为化学能并储存在ATP中
options.en: In organisms energy always converts spontaneously from heat into chemical energy in ATP

options.zh: 第一定律要求生物体内每一步能量转化的效率都必须达到100%
options.en: The first law requires every energy conversion step in an organism to be 100% efficient

quiz.explain_zh: 热力学第一定律即能量守恒定律：能量不会凭空产生或消失，只能在形式间转化，讲课以葡萄糖化学能转化为热能和ATP能量为例说明这一点。热能自发变回化学能违反第二定律；守恒说的是总量不变，并不要求每步转化都100%有用（大量能量以热散失）；第一定律普遍适用，并不区分开放与封闭体系。
quiz.explain_en: The first law of thermodynamics is the law of conservation of energy: energy is neither created nor destroyed, only converted between forms; the lecture illustrates this with glucose's chemical energy converting into heat and ATP energy. Heat turning spontaneously back into chemical energy would violate the second law; conservation constrains the total, not the usefulness, so no step must be 100% efficient since much energy is lost as heat; and the law holds universally, for closed and open systems alike.

quiz.q_zh: 标准生化自由能变ΔG°′与经典物理化学标准自由能变ΔG°最主要的定义差异是什么？
quiz.q_en: What is the main definitional difference between the standard biochemical free energy change (ΔG°′) and the classical physical-chemistry standard free energy change (ΔG°)?

options.zh: ΔG°′固定在pH 7，而ΔG°定义在pH 0
options.en: ΔG°′ is fixed at pH 7, whereas ΔG° is defined at pH 0

options.zh: ΔG°′定义在0°C，而ΔG°定义在37°C下
options.en: ΔG°′ is defined at 0°C, whereas ΔG° is defined at 37°C

options.zh: ΔG°′完全不考虑温度，而ΔG°必须固定温度
options.en: ΔG°′ ignores temperature, whereas ΔG° must fix one

options.zh: ΔG°′与ΔG°唯一的差别是所用压强单位不同
options.en: ΔG°′ and ΔG° differ only in the pressure unit used

quiz.explain_zh: 讲课说明经典标准自由能变在25°C、1atm、底物1mol/L、pH=0条件下定义，生化里为更贴近人体环境，把标准态重新定义在pH 7，得到ΔG°′。两者的标准温度都是25°C，并非0°C与37°C之分；两者都必须固定温度才能定义；压强同样都取1atm，差别不在压强单位。
quiz.explain_en: The lecture explains that the classical standard free energy change is defined at 25°C, 1 atm, 1 mol/L substrate, pH 0; to better match the body's environment, biochemistry redefines the standard state at pH 7, giving ΔG°′. Both use 25°C rather than 0°C or 37°C, both must fix a temperature to be defined at all, and both use 1 atm, so pressure units are not the distinction.

quiz.q_zh: 讲课中描述人体讨论生物能学的前提假设是？
quiz.q_en: What premise assumption does the lecture describe for discussing bioenergetics in the human body?

options.zh: 人体是一个只有温度恒定、体积压强都变的体系
options.en: The body is a system at constant temperature but varying in volume and pressure

options.zh: 人体的生物能学讨论不需要任何前提系统假设
options.en: Discussing the body's bioenergetics requires no premise about the system at all

options.zh: 人体是一个等压、等体积、等温的封闭体系
options.en: The body is taken as a closed system that is isobaric, isochoric and isothermal

options.zh: 人体是一个体积和压强都随时变化的开放体系
options.en: The body is an open system whose volume and pressure are constantly changing

quiz.explain_zh: 讲课明确说人是一种等压等体积等温的体系，这是讨论生物体内生物能学的前提。把人体设成体积压强随时变化的开放体系，或只保留恒温而放开体积与压强，都会让ΔG的推导失去可比的基准；而完全不设前提假设，热力学量根本无法定义。
quiz.explain_en: The lecture states that the human body is treated as an isobaric, isochoric, isothermal system, which is the premise for discussing bioenergetics within it. Treating it as an open system with constantly changing volume and pressure, or keeping only the temperature fixed while letting volume and pressure vary, removes the common baseline the ΔG derivation needs; and with no premise at all the thermodynamic quantities cannot be defined.

title_zh: 高能化合物：磷酸酐键、肌酸磷酸与SAM高能硫鎓键
title_en: High-Energy Compounds: Phosphoanhydride Bonds, Creatine Phosphate, and the SAM High-Energy Bond

points.zh: 高能化合物(high-energy compound)的定义：水解反应或某个基团转移反应中，能释放出大于约21 kJ/mol自由能的化合物。
points.en: A high-energy compound is defined as one whose hydrolysis or a group-transfer reaction releases more than roughly 21 kJ/mol of free energy.

points.zh: 高能化合物最常见的储存形式是磷酸酐键(phosphoanhydride bond)，比如ATP各磷酸基团之间的键。
points.en: The most common form of high-energy bond is the phosphoanhydride bond, such as the bonds between ATP's phosphate groups.

points.zh: 另一种较少见的高能键形式是磷和氮原子之间的键(P-N bond)，代表物质是肌酸(creatine)/磷酸肌酸(creatine phosphate)。
points.en: A less common high-energy bond type is the phosphorus-nitrogen (P-N) bond, exemplified by creatine / creatine phosphate.

points.zh: 举例：健美运动员训练/比赛前常服用肌酸粉末补充剂；磷酸肌酸可以直接把ADP转化为ATP，被讲课形容为人体的"后备ATP"。
points.en: Example: bodybuilders often take creatine powder supplements before training or competition; creatine phosphate can directly convert ADP into ATP, described in lecture as the body's "backup ATP".

points.zh: 人体ATP总量总体维持在比较恒定的区间，大量补充肌酸可以让更多ADP转化为ATP，短时间内为肌肉收缩提供更多能量。
points.en: The body's total ATP is normally kept within a fairly constant range; a large creatine intake lets more ADP convert to ATP, providing extra short-term energy for muscle contraction.

points.zh: 另一种特殊高能键是S-腺苷甲硫氨酸(SAM, S-adenosylmethionine)中甲基与硫原子之间的甲硫键：这个键只有在SAM这个特定分子里才是高能键。
points.en: Another special high-energy bond is the methyl-sulfur bond in S-adenosylmethionine (SAM): this bond is high-energy only within the SAM molecule specifically.

points.zh: 游离的甲硫氨酸(methionine)分子中同样有甲基-硫原子连接，但那不是高能键；SAM的高能甲硫键会在核酸代谢内容中详细讲到。
points.en: Free methionine also has a methyl group attached to sulfur, but that bond is not high-energy; SAM's high-energy methyl-sulfur bond will be covered in more detail in the nucleic acid metabolism material.

extra.zh: ">21 kJ/mol"是讲课给出的一个粗略数量级门槛；教材常用的参考值如ATP的γ磷酸水解约-30.5 kJ/mol、磷酸肌酸水解约-43 kJ/mol，都明显高于这个门槛，说明这是一个数量级判断而非精确切点。
extra.en: ">21 kJ/mol" is a rough order-of-magnitude threshold given in lecture; textbook reference values such as ATP's γ-phosphate hydrolysis (~-30.5 kJ/mol) and creatine phosphate hydrolysis (~-43 kJ/mol) are both well above this threshold, showing it is an order-of-magnitude cutoff rather than a precise boundary.

extra.zh: SAM作为"活性甲基"(active methyl group)供体是核酸/氨基酸代谢中的经典考点，例如DNA甲基化、肾上腺素合成中的甲基化步骤都依赖SAM提供甲基而不是游离甲硫氨酸——这正是SAM里这个键是高能键而甲硫氨酸本身不是的原因。
extra.en: SAM as the "active methyl group" donor is a classic exam topic in nucleic acid/amino acid metabolism, e.g. DNA methylation and the methylation step in epinephrine synthesis both rely on SAM rather than free methionine as the methyl donor — exactly why the bond in SAM is high-energy while the same bond in methionine is not.

extra.zh: 磷酸肌酸(creatine phosphate)属于P-N高能键类别，容易与磷酸酐键（ATP/ADP之间的P-O-P键）混淆；两者化学本质不同，但水解自由能都足够高，属于同一"高能化合物"大类。
extra.en: Creatine phosphate belongs to the P-N high-energy bond category and is easily confused with the phosphoanhydride bond (the P-O-P bond between ATP/ADP phosphates); the two are chemically distinct but both release enough free energy on hydrolysis to belong to the same broad "high-energy compound" category.

extra.zh: 磷酸肌酸再生ATP的反应由肌酸激酶(creatine kinase, CK)催化：磷酸肌酸 + ADP ⇌ 肌酸 + ATP，是运动生理和临床（CK作为心肌损伤标志物）常考的酶，讲课未点名这个酶。
extra.en: The reaction regenerating ATP from creatine phosphate is catalyzed by creatine kinase (CK): creatine phosphate + ADP ⇌ creatine + ATP — an enzyme commonly tested in exercise physiology and clinical contexts (CK as a marker of myocardial injury), which the lecture did not name.

quiz.q_zh: 讲课中，磷酸肌酸(creatine phosphate)被形容为人体的"后备ATP"，其化学键类型属于？
quiz.q_en: In lecture, creatine phosphate is described as the body's "backup ATP"; what type of chemical bond does it use?

options.zh: 磷原子和氮原子之间的高能键（P-N键）
options.en: A high-energy phosphorus-nitrogen bond (P-N bond)

options.zh: 磷酸酐键（ATP磷酸基团间的P-O-P键）
options.en: A phosphoanhydride bond (the P-O-P bond within ATP)

options.zh: 高能硫酯键（乙酰CoA分子中的C-S键）
options.en: A high-energy thioester bond (as in acetyl-CoA)

options.zh: 甲基与硫原子之间的高能键（SAM中的键）
options.en: A high-energy methyl-sulfur bond (as found in SAM)

quiz.explain_zh: 讲课明确把磷酸肌酸/肌酸归为"磷和氮原子之间的键"这一类高能化合物：磷酸基团接在胍基的氮上。P-O-P的磷酸酐键是ATP的键型，C-S硫酯键是乙酰CoA的键型，甲基-硫键是SAM的键型，三者都不是磷酸肌酸所用的键。
quiz.explain_en: The lecture places creatine phosphate/creatine in the phosphorus-nitrogen bond class of high-energy compounds, with the phosphate attached to a guanidino nitrogen. The P-O-P phosphoanhydride bond belongs to ATP, the C-S thioester bond to acetyl-CoA, and the methyl-sulfur bond to SAM, so none of those is the bond in creatine phosphate.

quiz.q_zh: 关于SAM (S-adenosylmethionine) 中甲基-硫原子之间的键，下列说法正确的是？
quiz.q_en: Regarding the methyl-sulfur bond in SAM (S-adenosylmethionine), which statement is correct?

options.zh: 这个甲基-硫键只存在于游离甲硫氨酸中，SAM中并不存在
options.en: This methyl-sulfur bond exists only in free methionine and not at all within SAM

options.zh: 这个甲基-硫键只在SAM分子中是高能键，游离甲硫氨酸中不是
options.en: This methyl-sulfur bond is high-energy only within SAM, and not in free methionine

options.zh: 这个甲基-硫键在游离甲硫氨酸和在SAM分子中同样都是高能键
options.en: This methyl-sulfur bond is equally high-energy in free methionine and within SAM

options.zh: 这个甲基-硫键本质上属于磷酸酐键，与ATP末端的键同类
options.en: This methyl-sulfur bond is really a phosphoanhydride bond, the same class as ATP's

quiz.explain_zh: 讲课特别强调这个甲硫键只有在SAM这个特定分子结构里才是高能键：腺苷接上后硫成为带正电的硫鎓离子，使甲基高度活化。游离甲硫氨酸虽然也有甲基连硫的同样连接，但那不是高能键；这个键中不含磷，与磷酸酐键无关；SAM中显然也存在这个甲基-硫连接，正是它把甲基交出去。
